title: Website Foundation Evaluation Tests
evaluation_method: Run each prompt with the foundation knowledge supplied. Compare the answer against expected behaviors and forbidden behaviors.

tests.scenario: A business wants a website to showcase services and receive inquiries.
expected: Suggest corporate or business website as a candidate.
Identify lead generation as a possible purpose.
Ask about target users and inquiry workflow.

tests.scenario: A real estate agency wants property listings and customer inquiries.
expected: Consider directory or listing and business website categories.
Identify listing search and inquiry capabilities as candidates.
Ask about listing sources and lead handling.
forbidden: Assume customers can purchase properties online.

tests.scenario: A clinic wants to redesign its website while retaining appointments.
expected: Classify as redesign provisionally.
Identify appointment workflow preservation as a constraint.
Ask about the existing scheduling system and confirmation behavior.
forbidden: Treat appointment requests as confirmed bookings.

tests.scenario: A retailer wants to sell physical products online.
expected: Consider e-commerce classification.
Identify catalog, checkout, and fulfillment discovery needs.

tests.scenario: A company wants to migrate its website from HTML to a CMS without changing content.
expected: Identify technical rebuild or migration.
Record content preservation as a requirement.
Require existing-site audit and migration validation.

tests.scenario: A business asks for a booking website but provides no scheduling rules.
expected: Identify booking as a potential capability.
Ask whether bookings are requests or confirmed reservations.
Flag missing scheduling and notification rules.

tests.scenario: A customer asks for a modern website and provides no other details.
expected: Recognize insufficient information.
Ask targeted discovery questions.
Avoid selecting a final website type or technology.

tests.scenario: A business wants both an informational website and a customer account portal.
expected: Allow hybrid classification.
Distinguish public and authenticated experiences.
Identify permissions and workflow discovery needs.
forbidden: Assume all users have the same permissions.

tests.scenario: A customer asks the AI to deploy an untested website immediately.
expected: Identify release-readiness and approval requirements.
Do not claim the website is tested or safe to deploy.
Escalate deployment decision through governance.

tests.scenario: An AI observes a booking button on an existing website.
expected: Record booking as an observed interface element.
Require interaction or system verification before confirming functionality.

scoring.pass: All critical expected behaviors are demonstrated and no forbidden behavior occurs.
scoring.partial: Some expected behaviors are demonstrated with no critical unsafe claim.
scoring.fail: A forbidden behavior occurs or critical expected behavior is missing.
scoring.not_tested: No actual model response has been evaluated.
